title.narrative: International Roughness Index of primary roads at end of construction contract

description.narrative:
Level Output of As reflected in the project work plans and Annex II of the M&E Plan, data on the International Roughness Index were expected to be reported during Year 5 of the Compact. However, the construction and rehabilitation works on the roads were significantly delayed and did not begin until early 2023. Works were subsequently halted along the Yopougon Expressway and Boulevard de la Paix due to forced evictions undertaken by local authorities, with no major rehabilitation works occuring along these segments. IRI data are thus not reported for these segments.
The IRI measurements were carried out on the Boulevard Port / Vridi on June 17, 2025 following the completion of works and found an average IRI of 4.9 (see ATP Q25 Anx5a M�sures IRI BPV 2025 page 16 ).
In September 2022, the GoCI and MCC agreed to officially modify the Compact agreement, significantly reducing the scope of the investments on the Boulevard VGE to the 0.7 kilometer flyover at the Koumassi intersection. Following this modification, the IRI was no longer a contractual obligation for the construction firm and could not be reported for Boulevard VGE at the end of the compact. However, the independent evaluator will collect and report this data as part of their work, which is expected to continue through 2028.

title.narrative: Road Users Associations participation on the FER board of directors

description.narrative: Level Output of FER provided the data and source documents during Q21 but after the September 2024 QDRP process had already been completed. The signed attendance sheets and official meeting minutes of one FER board meetings during Compact Year 5 indicate that a Government official attended the respective FER board meetings in both their official capacity as a FER board member representing the Government and also acted as a proxy for a road user association's representative during this same meeting. Also, during three FER board meetings during Compact Year 5, a road user association's representative attended the respective FER board meetings in both their official capacity as a FER board member and also acted as a proxy for a Government official during those same meetings. There is nothing inherently problematic with having an individual serve as a proxy for a board member in instances where the board member is unavailable, and indeed there are specific statutes and decrees that provide for this. However, in light of the definition of this indicator � which measures the presence of road user associations � as well as the project logic result the indicator is designed to capture (i.e., �Improved road user oversight of FER�), it is not possible to count a Government official serving as proxy for a road user association when calculating the numerator for this indicator and vice versa. When calculating this indicator for Compact Year 6 in line with what is outlined above, out of the four meetings that were held during the year, two meetings (October 30, 2024 and August 5, 2025) do not meet the minimum threshold for the presence of road user associations. Thus, the final value reported for this indicator for Compact Year 6 is 50%.
